evidence: With a dummy Triton kernel that writes per-token losses into the loss buffer, LigerFusedLinearCrossEntropyLoss(reduction='none') still returns a scalar tensor with shape torch.Size([]).
steps: Created a clean Python 3.12 virtualenv and installed CPU PyTorch, Triton, and packaging.
Loaded the local fused linear cross entropy implementation directly from codebase/src.
Monkeypatched the Triton kernel with a CPU stub that writes a distinct value per token into the loss buffer.
Called LigerFusedLinearCrossEntropyLoss(reduction='none') on a small CPU tensor input.
Observed that the returned loss was scalar instead of a 1D tensor of unreduced losses.
